notes:
29 stations, lines 286-321, under the overall heading "EAST OF SCOTLAND" and printed in three groups: Shetland. (4-7), Orkney. (8-14) and Mainland. (15-29, including 26B and 28B). No keepers are named in the list, as line 276 says.

Conventions used:
- Fragments are each line's text exactly as printed, with only the leading indentation and trailing spaces removed. Spacing inside a line is kept, so the left-hand count columns are part of the fragment.
- The number is given without the period that follows it ("4." is given as "4", "26B." as "26B").
- Names keep the comma that follows them, to match your "Farn, Inner," example. Places drop the comma that separates them from the Values column.
- In "other", the four numeric columns are labelled from the column headers: Schedules filled in 1887; Returns in 9 years incl. 1887; Values; Feet.
- The * is put in marks. It sits in the "1887. Actual returns." column and means actual returns in 1887.

Column reading:
- I assigned the counts by where they sit under the headers. Auskerry's 6, Cromarty's 6, Chanonry Point's 4 and Fidra's 2 are in the returns-in-9-years column, not the schedules column.
- Buchan Ness and Girdleness have "1st" in the returns column, apparently meaning their first year of returns.
- Bell Rock's schedules entry is "1 (one lost)". Isle of May has "0" schedules and no *.
- Many rows have no counts at all. Sumburgh Head and all the Orkney rows have no height (Feet blank).
- The "Values" (Roman numerals I-V) aren't explained in this passage. They aren't light characters, so they go in "other", not "character".

Two-line rows:
- 26B Carr Rock (lines 315-316). "Lightship" is printed at the start of the second line, and I put it in type. It is the only row with a type.
- 28B Fidra (lines 319-320). "Firth of / Forth" is split across the two lines, and I gave the place as "Firth of Forth". "instituted 1886" goes in "other". Both rows have "?" for Values and Feet.

Possible errors, all left as printed:
- "Whalsey Skerries" (usually Whalsay).
- "N. Ronaldshay".
- "Girdleness" and "Montroseness" written as one word.
- Some places look wrong. Chanonry Point is given as Elgin, but it is on the Black Isle in Ross-shire. Montroseness is given as Aberdeen, but Montrose is in Forfarshire. Cromarty's place is "East Cromarty". Bell Rock and Carr Rock are both "Fife Coast"; that is reasonable for Carr Rock, but Bell Rock lies off Angus.
- "Dunnet Head,  Caithness," has two spaces before Caithness. I kept them in the fragment.
